title: The Unabridged Journals of Sylvia Plath

vibeProfile.oneLine: A great poet's private journals, ambition and anguish laid bare.

summary: Plath's private journals, published unabridged, run from her college years to shortly before her death, recording in astonishing, unfiltered prose her ambition, rage, love, self-doubt and ferocious will to write. They are a rare, close-up look at a major artist making herself, page by page, alongside a vivid record of a woman's inner life in the 1950s and early 60s. Raw and brilliant, they are as compelling as any of her published work, and often more revealing.
whyReadIt: An astonishing, unfiltered window into a great poet making herself. As gripping as any novel, and more revealing.

funFacts.text: Her husband Ted Hughes said he destroyed the final journal; the rest were published in full in 2000.
